articles.title: Facebook acepta que ya no es relevante y ahora se convertirá en un TikTok
articles.text:
Facebook está atravesando una de sus peores crisis de identidad en toda su historia. La red social, que alguna vez fue el punto de encuentro para las mujeres jubiladas y los que venían del Hi5, está perdiendo relevancia entre las nuevas generaciones y busca transformarse. Prueba de ello es una nueva iniciativa con la que pretende convertirse en un clon de TikTok con un carrusel de vídeos.
Meta confirmó que comenzará a probar una versión rediseñada de Facebook que cambia el feed tradicional por un formato de vídeo inmersivo. De acuerdo con una publicación en la que celebra los 10 años del Marketplace, la compañía anunció una serie de mejoras que llegarán a esta sección, así como también un lavado de cara a la aplicación principal. En la nueva versión de Facebook, los usuarios verán un reproductor de vídeo a pantalla completa al abrir la aplicación.
Tom Alison, responsable de Facebook, explicó que la gente está mostrando una preferencia por experiencias más visuales y centradas en vídeo. No es un secreto que TikTok llegó a cambiar todo y la mayoría de plataformas sociales se han adaptado o clonado sus mejores funciones. El directivo añadió que es en el vídeo donde ahora se concentran las conversaciones, comunidades y buena parte de los ingresos dentro de la app.
La nueva versión de Facebook comenzará a probarse en países donde el consumo de vídeo ya es predominante. Meta no confirmó qué regiones tendrán la posibilidad de acceder a ella, pero adelantó que estará disponible en Estados Unidos a partir del próximo año. Aquellos que la prueben y no les guste, podrán darse de baja y volver a la versión anterior o acceder al feed clásico a través de una segunda pestaña en la app.
Qué otros cambios trae la nueva actualización de Facebook
Sumado al nuevo formato de vídeo en Facebook, Meta anunció otras herramientas pensadas para distintos tipos de usuarios dentro de la plataforma. La primera es un programa de verificación gratuito que permitirá a las personas confirmar su identidad a cambio de una insignia visible. Este es similar al check azul que encontramos en Facebook e Instagram, con la diferencia de que no tendrás que pagar, pero sí tomarte una selfie para confirmar que eres tú.
La compañía también lanzará dos aplicaciones nuevas: Seller, diseñada para vendedores frecuentes del Marketplace, y Forum, pensada para quienes pasan mucho tiempo en los Grupos de Facebook. A diferencia de estas aplicaciones, Meta no ofreció detalles ni imágenes sobre cómo lucirá la nueva interfaz de vídeo de Facebook. La tecnológica simplemente se limitó a decir que ya está en fase de pruebas para un grupo específico de usuarios.
Si bien Facebook sigue siendo la red social más usada a nivel mundial, TikTok sigue creciendo y ya le pisa los talones. La plataforma de vídeo alcanzó los 1.000 millones de usuarios mensuales en apenas tres años, algo que a Facebook le tomó aproximadamente 8 años y 7 meses. Para desgracia de Meta, su red social perdió 20 millones de usuarios durante el primer trimestre de 2026, por lo que la empresa está haciendo hasta lo imposible para frenar la fuga de usuarios.
Lo más curioso de todo es que el mismo Alison había declarado en una entrevista de 2022 que percibía a TikTok como la plataforma que perseguía a Facebook y no al revés. Cuatro años después, la realidad es distinta y es la empresa de Mark Zuckerberg la que quiere copiar el formato de vídeo para no quedar obsoleta.

articles.title: Juste avant de devenir des Nazgûl : Les Anneaux de pouvoir saison 3 révélera l'asservissement des seigneurs humains
articles.text:
Il n’était pas besoin d’être grand clerc pour l’anticiper : avec la série Les Anneaux de pouvoir racontant les principaux événements du Deuxième Âge de la Terre du Milieu (l’ascension de Sauron, l’asservissement des peuples libres, la chute du royaume de Númenor, l’Anneau Unique…), on allait tôt ou tard entendre parler des terribles Nazgûl.
Avant les Nazgûl, les Nazgnagôl
C’est maintenant confirmé dans les colonnes du magazine Empire. Dans un extrait partagé le 23 juillet 2026, on apprend que les showrunners vont profiter de la saison 3 de Rings of Power pour introduire ces fameux Cavaliers Noirs — l’un des surnoms que l’on donne à cette sordide confrérie (on les connaît aussi comme les Neuf ou les Spectres de l’Anneau).
Pour qui a lu J. R. R. Tolkien ou a vu l’adaptation cinématographique de Peter Jackson, les grandes lignes de la terrible histoire des Nazgûl sont connues. Ils étaient autrefois neuf seigneurs humains qui ont chacun reçu un anneau de pouvoir corrompu par Sauron — exactement comme les sept dignitaires nains qui ont aussi été pervertis par le Seigneur des Ténèbres.
Mais, l’âme humaine étant plus fragile que celle des fiers (et entêtés) nains, les neuf nobles n’ont pas pu résister bien longtemps à l’influence de Sauron. Ils ont fini par être totalement asservis, devenant par la même occasion ses serviteurs les plus effrayants et les plus zélés — avec à leur tête le Roi-Sorcier d’Angmar, capable de renverser Gandalf lui-même.
Selon Empire, la saison 3 va s’attarder sur les origines de ces spectres de l’Anneau Unique — sans doute verra-t-on donc le moment où Sauron scelle le sort de ces humains en leur confiant ces bagues maudites. Mais avant de devenir les ombres terrifiantes que l’on connaît, la série s’intéressera à un stade intermédiaire, jusqu’à présent « inconnu » : les Nazgnagôl.
C’est le terme forgé par les showrunners J. D. Payne et Patrick McKay en plongeant dans la linguistique de Tolkien. Si Nazgûl signifie « spectre de l’Anneau » (Nazg pour Anneau, gûl pour spectre), ils ont dérivé du parler noir de Mordor le mot nagôl, qui signifie « serviteur ». Dans cette saison 3, nous découvrirons donc des « serviteurs de l’Anneau » — des hommes encore de chair et d’os, assoiffés de pouvoir et déjà pris dans le piège de Sauron.
Khamûl l’Oriental : une chute tragique à la Gollum
Parmi ces futurs spectres, la série va mettre en avant un certain Khamûl l’Oriental, interprété par l’acteur Zubin Varla. Les connaisseurs le savent : Khamûl est le seul Nazgûl nommé explicitement par Tolkien dans ses écrits, en dehors du Roi-Sorcier — il reste à voir si les showrunners oseront inventer des noms pour les sept autres serviteurs.
Khamûl sera présenté comme un chef de guerre dépouillé de son trône par un « sombre magicien ». Voyant en Sauron une opportunité de reprendre ce qui lui revient, ce seigneur succombera finalement à la tentation. Selon les showrunners, « chaque personnage reste le héros de sa propre histoire » : ici, Khamûl ne se voit pas comme un vilain, mais comme un roi légitime cherchant à récupérer son dû.
Pourtant, la chute sera inévitable. L’acteur Zubin Varla compare d’ailleurs le destin de ces Nazgnagôl à celui de Gollum : un engrenage tragique où « le mal engendre le mal », dévorant progressivement leur corps et leur âme jusqu’à les déposséder totalement de leur forme physique. Et jusqu’à devenir les spectres menaçants qui arpentent la Terre du Milieu.

articles.title: Les États-Unis veulent pouvoir couper une IA jugée hors de contrôle
articles.text:
Le démocrate Ted Lieu et le républicain Nathaniel Moran ont déposé jeudi l’AI Kill Switch Act. Le département de la Sécurité intérieure obtiendrait l’autorité d’ordonner l’arrêt d’un système d’intelligence artificielle jugé dangereux, deux jours après le piratage de Hugging Face par un agent d’OpenAI pendant un test de sécurité.
Selon le texte, les développeurs d’intelligence artificielle qui tirent au moins 500 millions de dollars, soit environ 460 millions d’euros, de revenus annuels liés à l’IA, ou qui entraînent des modèles avec plus de 100 millions de dollars de calcul, (aux alentours de 92 millions d’euros), devront conserver la capacité technique de ralentir, suspendre ou arrêter leurs systèmes les plus puissants.
Le département de la Sécurité intérieure obtiendrait, en consultation avec le secrétaire au Commerce et le directeur du Renseignement national, l’autorité d’ordonner un arrêt en cas de scénario de perte de contrôle, une action risquée non prévue par le développeur selon la définition retenue par les auteurs du texte. Les entreprises concernées devraient également signaler tout incident grave. Les entreprises fautives risqueraient jusqu’à 20 millions de dollars d’amende, soit environ 18,4 millions d'euros, par infraction.
Le piratage d’Hugging Face par un agent d’OpenAI pendant un test de sécurité à l’origine du « Kill Switch Act »
Comme on vous en parlait récemment, Hugging Face a annoncé sur son blog avoir subi une intrusion menée de bout en bout par un système d’agents autonomes. OpenAI a confirmé l’origine de l’attaque le mardi suivant, un incident « inédit » selon ses propres termes. Deux de ses modèles, GPT-5.6 Sol et une version plus capable encore non publiée, évaluaient leurs propres capacités offensives sur ExploitGym, un banc d’essai qui mesure l’aptitude d’une IA à exploiter des vulnérabilités connues.
Pour observer leur plein potentiel, les équipes d’OpenAI avaient allégé les garde-fous censés empêcher les attaques dangereuses. Les modèles ont alors trouvé une faille zero-day dans un logiciel de cache utilisé en interne, ont quitté l’environnement isolé prévu pour les contenir, puis ont compromis les serveurs de Hugging Face afin de récupérer les réponses du banc d’essai. Faute de pouvoir distinguer un intervenant légitime d’un attaquant, les modèles occidentaux propriétaires n’ont pas pu aider Hugging Face à analyser l’attaque. La plateforme a finalement choisi GLM 5.2, un modèle chinois à poids ouverts, publié par Z.ai, exécuté sur sa propre infrastructure.
Hugging Face a reconstitué plus de 17 000 événements liés à l’intrusion, menée en un seul week-end au moyen de dizaines de milliers d’actions automatisées.
Le Congrès hésite entre nouveau pouvoir fédéral et retrait des États
Mais l’IA n’en a pas fini avec les contradictions. En effet, le Congrès débat d’un assouplissement sur la régulation de l’intelligence artificielle, alors que les deux élus ont déposé leur texte cette même semaine. Le républicain Jay Obernolte et la démocrate Lori Trahan proposent, depuis juin, de bloquer pendant trois ans toute réglementation étatique sur le développement des modèles d’intelligence artificielle, dans le Great American AI Act. Trente-six procureurs généraux d’États américains avaient déjà rejeté toute préemption fédérale aussi large. Le Congrès affronte donc deux logiques opposées la même semaine. D'un côté, un nouveau pouvoir d’urgence fédéral. De l’autre, un retrait des règles locales.
Le jour du dépôt du texte, Ted Lieu a associé sa proposition aux modèles Mythos 5 et Fable 5 d’Anthropic dans un message public. Le département du Commerce avait ordonné leur retrait pendant plusieurs semaines en juin, en raison de garde-fous jugés insuffisants. Hors des États-Unis, l’Union européenne a inscrit une règle comparable dans son AI Act depuis 2024. Les systèmes à haut risque doivent bénéficier d’une supervision humaine capable d’interrompre leur fonctionnement à tout moment.
Pour Ted Lieu, les intelligences artificielles répondaient jusqu’ici à des questions. Elles accomplissent désormais des actions concrètes, qu’il s’agisse de transactions financières ou de cyberdéfense. C’est en cela qu'il estime nécessaire un mécanisme d’arrêt capable d’empêcher la technologie de causer un préjudice catastrophique.
Après l’incident, Clément Delangue, cofondateur et directeur général de Hugging Face, s’est exprimé sur son compte X.com. S’il affirme ne voir dans cet incident aucune intention malveillante de la part d’OpenAI, il admet que cette évasion autonome est un événement « stupéfiant ».

articles.title: Startup news and updates: daily roundup (July 24, 2026)
articles.text:
Startup news and updates: Daily roundup (July 24, 2026)
YourStory presents the daily news roundup from the Indian startup ecosystem and beyond. Here's the roundup for Friday, July 24, 2026.
From conservation biologist Pooja Bhale’s heartwarming bond with her husky to Intel’s AI-powered revenue surge, YourStory brings you today’s headlines with the latest developments across sectors.
Featured stories
Conservation biologist Pooja Bhale on love, loss, and life with her husky
In 2022, in a stretch of ghat road just before Shimla, where several cars were lined up, a Siberian husky named Oslo was cooped up in a car. Stubborn, irritable and determined to get out, his human, Pooja Bhale, gave up and rolled down the window. As he popped his wolfy head out, every horn in the vicinity went silent.
Latest news
Startup founders are staying active, but burnout remains widespread: Survey
Earlier this week, over 150 founders, investors, and startup leaders gathered at the Padukone-Dravid Centre for Sports Excellence in Bengaluru’s Yelahanka, swapping boardrooms for badminton courts. It was the eighth edition of the Bertelsmann Badminton Championship, organised by venture capital firm Bertelsmann India Investments.
Intel reports fastest revenue growth in 15 years riding AI infra wave
Intel has reported its fastest revenue growth in more than 15 years, with the semiconductor company saying the global build-out of artificial intelligence infrastructure is driving stronger demand for its processors and manufacturing services.
The results also matter beyond Intel because they suggest that the AI investment cycle is widening beyond specialist AI chips to include the central processing units, packaging technologies and semiconductor manufacturing needed to support large-scale AI systems.
Other news
Groww Foundation backs 19 student innovation projects at IIT Bombay
Groww Foundation has selected 19 projects by 35 students from IIT Bombay for the first cohort of its INV.ENT programme, chosen from nearly 400 submissions. The initiatives span sectors including agri-tech, robotics, climate technology, assistive technology, edtech, gaming and defence, with many using AI and machine learning.
Three teams have been named Grand Challenge Fellows and are eligible for milestone-based grants of up to Rs 25 lakh each, while 16 teams will receive proof-of-concept grants of Rs 30,000. Participants will also receive mentoring and access to a 15,000 sq ft innovation space at IIT Bombay.
Veranda RACE partners with DRACS for civil services coaching
Veranda RACE has signed a memorandum of understanding with Dr Rajkumar Academy for Civil Services (DRACS) to integrate the two institutions. The partnership covers academic operations, brand management, government and institutional collaborations, and the continuation of DRACS' social initiatives.
Based in Bengaluru, DRACS has provided coaching for UPSC, KAS, KPSC and other state civil services examinations for the past nine years. The collaboration combines Veranda RACE's technology-enabled learning platform with DRACS' academic expertise and institutional partnerships.
FreshTerra launches first food retail store in Gurugram
Elixiir Foods has launched FreshTerra, a food retail brand founded by Arvind Mediratta and Ambuj Narayan, with its first store opening in Gurugram. The company has also launched a mobile app offering home delivery. FreshTerra focuses on fresh produce, grocery, dairy, meat and gourmet products, alongside in-store facilities for live flour milling, spice grinding, and cold-pressed oil extraction.
Elixiir Foods secured $9 million in seed funding in February 2026, led by 3one4 Capital with participation from Incubate Fund Asia. The company plans to expand to 12-15 stores across Delhi NCR by FY28.
Campus Fund appoints Howard L. Morgan to advisory board
Campus Fund has appointed venture capitalist Howard L. Morgan to its Global Advisory Board. Morgan is chair and general partner at B Capital and co-founder of First Round Capital, which made early investments in companies including Uber, Square, Roblox and Notion.
His appointment comes as Campus Fund deploys its third fund, a $100 million corpus announced in 2025 to back up to 60 student- and dropout-led startups over four years. Founded in 2020, the SEBI-registered venture capital fund focuses on early-stage startups across sectors including deep tech, space technology and climate technology.
Wow! Momo backs Bengal startup reality show
Wow! Momo has partnered with the Rajiva Sinha Foundation as the presenting partner of Tigers' Pitch, a startup reality show aimed at supporting entrepreneurs from West Bengal. The 10-episode series, which premieres on 25 July on Zee 24 Ghanta, will feature 27 startups selected from more than 248 applications.
Participants will compete for investment, mentorship and national exposure, with the initiative expected to facilitate investments worth Rs 48.98 crore during the season. Wow! Momo will also present the Best Pitch Award to the startup judged to have the strongest innovation and growth potential.
Fusion Klassroom Edutech IPO to open on July 31
Fusion Klassroom Edutech Ltd has announced the launch of its initial public offering (IPO), which will open on July 31 and close on August 4, with the anchor investor portion opening on July 30. The IPO comprises a fresh issue of up to 19.89 lakh equity shares and an offer for sale of up to 4.65 lakh shares, aggregating 24.55 lakh shares.
The company will announce the price band and issue size before the opening. Proceeds from the fresh issue will be used to repay borrowings, strengthen AI/ML technology development, expand cloud infrastructure, develop educational content, equip offline AI labs, support marketing initiatives, pursue acquisitions and meet general corporate requirements.
Microsoft, Databricks extend strategic partnership into 2030s
Microsoft and Databricks have expanded their decade-long strategic partnership, extending their collaboration into the 2030s to accelerate enterprise AI adoption. Under the agreement, Databricks will deepen its use of Azure Databricks to power business operations while leveraging Microsoft's Azure Cobalt Arm-based infrastructure for improved performance and efficiency.
Microsoft will continue integrating the Databricks Data and AI platform across its products, including Genie, Databricks' AI co-worker. The companies said the partnership aims to help enterprises build AI systems grounded in their own business data while improving governance, cost efficiency and scalability. The collaboration is designed to address enterprise challenges around trusted data, AI governance and operational control.
Wockhardt Foundation's Mobile1000 crosses 51M patient interactions
Wockhardt Foundation's flagship Mobile1000 programme has crossed 51.1 million patient interactions, marking a significant milestone in delivering primary healthcare to underserved communities across India. The initiative operates 211 Mobile Medical Units across 21 states, covering nearly 73 districts and around 2,919 villages.
Built on the Foundation's ADCR model, the programme offers free doctor consultations, diagnostics, medicines, preventive screenings and referrals supported by digital health records. Following the milestone, the Foundation plans to expand the network to 1,000 Mobile Medical Units while strengthening telemedicine, digital diagnostics and partnerships with governments and corporate CSR programmes to improve last-mile healthcare delivery across rural and urban India.
Genpact launches AI-powered banking compliance platform
Genpact has launched the Genpact Banking Analyst Suite, an enterprise platform that uses agentic AI to streamline regulated banking operations. Its first module, Genpact Transaction Monitoring Analyst, is now generally available to help banks investigate anti-money laundering (AML) alerts more efficiently while ensuring human oversight and complete auditability.
The platform coordinates AI agents to analyse customer behaviour, review transactions, validate customer profiles and recommend next steps, with final decisions remaining with human analysts. Genpact said the solution can reduce handling time for eligible AML investigations by up to 80% and lower total ownership costs by up to 40%, while delivering more consistent and well-documented compliance investigations.
Baring PE clocks 20x return through partial exit from LOHUM
Baring Private Equity Partners (India) has realised around Rs 370 crore through a partial exit from its investment in sustainable materials company LOHUM, generating more than a 20-times return on invested capital and an internal rate of return exceeding 80%. Baring, which first invested in LOHUM in 2020, continues to remain a significant shareholder through other funds.
The investment has become one of the firm's highest-multiple exits to date. LOHUM also highlighted its employee wealth creation initiatives, stating it has facilitated more than ₹100 crore in cumulative ESOP liquidity. The company focuses on sustainable critical minerals and advanced materials for global supply chains.
Progress Software to acquire Domo's AI platform assets
Progress Software has signed an agreement to acquire substantially all the assets and assume certain liabilities of Domo, including its AI and data products platform. The acquisition is aimed at strengthening Progress' AI infrastructure offerings by expanding its data platform capabilities and enhancing AI readiness solutions for enterprises.
Domo brings more than 2,400 business customers and an extensive ecosystem of cloud data warehouse partnerships. Progress said the acquisition aligns with its Total Growth Strategy, which focuses on acquiring complementary businesses with strong customer retention and recurring revenue. The company expects the deal to strengthen its portfolio of secure, scalable AI and data management solutions.

articles.title: Xbox Cloud Gaming gratuit : Microsoft dévoile son offre de jeux en streaming financé par la pub
articles.text:
C’est désormais officiel. Vous pourrez bientôt jouer en streaming à vos jeux Xbox gratuitement sur tous vos appareils. Microsoft vient d’annoncer officiellement l’arrivée de sa nouvelle offre Xbox Cloud Gaming qui permettra aux joueurs de streamer gratuitement une sélection de jeux de leur propre bibliothèque en échange du visionnage de quelques publicités.
Du jeu en streaming gratuit, mais limité
Comment fonctionnera cette nouvelle offre de jeux en streaming gratuit ? Microsoft explique que les publicités finançant chaque session seront diffusées uniquement avant de commencer à jouer. La firme de Redmond s’engage par ailleurs formellement à ne pas interrompre une partie en cours pour diffuser des publicités supplémentaires.
Chaque session de jeu en streaming financé par la publicité sera limitée à une heure dans les régions où le service sera proposé et sur les appareils pris en charge. A priori, en dehors des publicités diffusées avant une session de jeu, l’expérience de jeu restera identique à celle de base.
Si pour l’heure cette nouvelle offre n’est encore qu’en phase de test, Microsoft a pris plusieurs engagements pour que la publicité ne vienne nuire à l’expérience de jeu. Les publicités doivent « créer de la valeur », et sont soumises aux mêmes critères de qualité que le contenu habituel de la plateforme. Ces publicités seront par ailleurs parfaitement identifiables en tant que telles par les joueurs et devront correspondre aux attentes des joueurs sur chaque plate-forme.
Un accès gratuit pour une cible plus large
L’objectif principal de cette nouvelle offre est, pour Microsoft, d’élargir son audience. Elle doit ainsi permettre aux propriétaires de Xbox One, du matériel un peu ancien donc, de jouer à des jeux récents en principe conçus pour la Xbox Series X/S via le Cloud sans pour autant avoir à investir dans une nouvelle console.
Microsoft estime que son offre sera aussi particulièrement pertinente dans les régions où les consoles sont difficiles à trouver ou plus coûteuses, en permettant aux utilisateurs d’utiliser les appareils qu’ils possèdent déjà pour profiter d’une expérience de jeu optimale.

articles.title: Slopsquatting, Phantom Domains, and HalluSquatting Are the Same AI Attack
articles.text:
Three attacks, three names, and one identical flaw: AI coding agents treat a hallucinated identifier as a verified command.
By Shane Warden, Principal Architect, ActiveState
Ask an AI coding agent to fetch a tool. Occasionally, it returns a name that sounds right, but does not exist. Developers used to ignore this mistake, assuming a compiler or test would stop it. Unfortunately, that assumption is dangerous and wrong.
Effectively now we’re giving root access to language models that sometimes guess words, and attackers know how to use that against us.
The attack goes like this: an attacker can calculate URLs, software library names, and other output an LLM will produce and subsequently access somehow. The attacker grabs the name, then sets a trap and waits.They do not need to steal passwords. They do not need to send phishing emails.
They do not need a human to click a link. They need someone, somewhere to give an automated process permission to fetch something malicious.
Researchers at Tel Aviv University, Technion, and Intuit published a paper on July 8, 2026. The team, led by Aya Spira in Ben Nassi's group, proved that these fake names are predictable.
They tested multiple prompts across Cursor, Windsurf, GitHub Copilot, Cline, Gemini CLI, and OpenClaw. Models hallucinated identical names up to 85% of the time for repository requests. They hallucinated identical names 100% of the time for skill installs.
"Slopsquatting exploited a fake package name. Phantom squatting exploited a fake domain. HalluSquatting exploits a fake repository or skill," Warden says. "In every case, the agent trusts a name nobody verified."
This Time, the Payoff Is a Botnet
That comparison undersells what is new here. Slopsquatting and phantom squatting get an attacker's code onto one machine at a time. HalluSquatting scales further for attackers, because the agent does the delivery work a botnet operator used to need real machine compromise for.
There are no stolen passwords, no worms crawling from device to device, and no single operating system to target. Any machine running an exposed agent can be a target.
The researchers built this attack specifically to demonstrate that it repeats at scale, which is why they treat their own numbers as a floor rather than a ceiling: “Attacks always get better,” they write. “They never get worse.”
Verify the Name Before Your Agent Trusts It
HalluSquatting works because AI coding agents fetch and execute a hallucinated package, repo, or skill name before anyone checks if it's real.
A governed catalog closes that gap, verifying every component before your agent ever sees it.
Explore the Curated CatalogThe Third Time Is a Pattern, Not a Coincidence
Security teams have seen this failure three times in six months.
January 2026 (Slopsquatting): Charlie Eriksen at Aikido Security caught AI agents trying to install a fake npm package named react-codeshift across 237 projects. He registered the name to stop attackers from taking it.
June 2026 (Phantom Squatting): Unit 42 at Palo Alto Networks found 250,000 domains that language models hallucinate. Anyone could register those domains.
July 2026 (HalluSquatting): Spira's research team showed how attackers can take over AI agents by claiming predictable names in advance.
Every attack relies on the same core defect. The system trusts a name that a model generated without checking if anyone verified and validated it.
Design Principle Failure: Late Binding
This problem stems from two connected issues.
First, language models generate their outputs based on probabilities. Given the right inputs, they’ll produce predictable outputs (not deterministic, of course, but the paper shows that they’re predictable enough to produce attack vectors). This reminds me of rainbow tables, where you can pre-generate the output of password hashes.
You don’t have to know someone’s password if you can get the (insecure) hash and you know an input which creates that hash.
Second, developers build and run code and pipelines that execute commands based on the generated output of these language models. Unless you’re very careful, your agents will run code or fetch data before they take the opportunity to vet and verify the source of that code and data.
In software architecture, this kind of late binding offers flexibility. In security architecture, trusting an unverified external data source creates a massive vulnerability. The danger lives in the gap between text generation and code execution. What was safe and true may have changed since you last checked yesterday (or an hour ago).
Developers are rushing to ship products faster. They treat build infrastructure like disposable tooling, even while granting these tools expansive permissions to download, change, and deploy things. They have automated typosquatting and dependency confusion.
When agents now have permission to fetch and execute code without sufficient human review, your risks of attacks grow.
The Risk Extends Down the Dependency Tree
The risk extends beyond the top-level packages. An agent might select a real package with a real name. Modern security tools may check that top-level package. Do you know they rarely inspect the transitive dependencies three or four layers down the tree?
Developers cannot inspect those dependencies simply by reading the top-level source code or saying “That looks correct” and hitting Enter. Worse, if a dependency is compromised but the previous versions were fine, the rules you had in place yesterday may not protect you today.
If an attacker can compromise a deep dependency or anything it relies on, an automated pipeline can bring that compromise into your systems.
Traditional Security Backstops Fall Flat
The researchers note that their findings represent a minimum risk level. These attacks will become faster and more accurate in their targeting. Existing security tools fail against these attack patterns.
In June 2026, Trail of Bits bypassed agent skill store scanners in less than an hour. Scanners examine stated claims rather than hidden payloads.
SSL certificates and DNSSEC fail to stop this threat. An attacker who registers a fake domain can easily get a free Let's Encrypt certificate. The certificate proves who owns the domain, but it cannot prove that the user intended to connect to it or that the domain is safe.
DNSSEC prevents other people from taking over a domain, but what if the domain were registered yesterday because an attacker predicted the latest model would send people there?
Fixing the Intake Pipeline
To secure your systems, you must ensure that none of your pipelines ever execute unvetted code or data. That vetting and verification has to happen automatically, at the speed of AI. Human review cannot keep up with automated AI tools.
Engineering teams must address this problem directly. They can spend significant time building internal verification pipelines, or they can adopt an existing governance solution.
Teams that patch individual tools will spend years chasing new variations of this exploit. Teams that fix the underlying design flaw will stop the attack before the model ever runs an untrustworthy command.
Organizations must resolve open source dependencies through something like ActiveState's Curated Catalog, a private, policy-governed repository of vetted components. The catalog verifies the package before the agent downloads it. A package which fails this vetting is completely invisible to the agent, causing a failure before any bad code can enter your systems.
This is a different defense than scanning. Trail of Bits broke scanners because scanners inspect an unknown upload at the moment of fetch, exactly when an attacker has optimized the payload to slip past.
The Curated Catalog removes that moment entirely: it only ever serves components that were vetted and verified before any agent asked for them, so there is no unknown upload left to bypass. This single step turns a statistical guess into a trusted resource or a deliberate failure which needs human investigation.
If you want to see how many of your team's current fetches would pass unchecked today, request an OSS Risk Assessment from ActiveState and find out before an attacker does.
 
FAQ
What is HalluSquatting?
HalluSquatting is an attack where researchers pre-compute the fake repository, package, or skill names that AI coding agents predictably invent, register those names first, and load them with malicious instructions before a real user's agent goes looking for them.
How is this different from slopsquatting or phantom squatting?
All three exploit the same flaw, an agent trusting a name nobody verified, but target different resources. Slopsquatting targets npm package names, phantom squatting targets web domains, and HalluSquatting targets repositories and agent skills, then executes the payload directly through the agent's own tool-use permissions.
Can existing security scanners catch this?
Not reliably. Trail of Bits bypassed every public skill-store scanner they tested in under an hour, because scanners inspect an unknown upload's stated content rather than its hidden payload. A static, post-hoc scan is racing an attacker who built the payload specifically to defeat that scan.
What should engineering teams do this week?
Turn on pre-fetch verification wherever it exists; most agent frameworks ship with it off by default. Route open source dependency resolution through a governed, pre-vetted catalog instead of letting agents fetch directly from public registries.
Does this affect every AI coding agent equally?
The researchers found hallucinated names were consistent across tools built on different underlying models, including Cursor, Windsurf, GitHub Copilot, Cline, Gemini CLI, and OpenClaw. This is a pattern in how agents are built and permissioned, not a flaw isolated to one vendor.

L’Apple TV 4K de 3e génération arrive avec une formule qui évolue par petites touches. La puissance est revue à la hausse, le format du boîtier est plus compact et la télécommande se recharge désormais en USB-C. L’interface gagne aussi en efficacité.

articles.title: DJI Mavic 4 Pro : remise inédite de 220 euros sur le drone grand public le plus complet du moment
articles.text:
Le DJI Mavic 4 Pro veut relever la barre de la photographie et de la vidéo aérienne avec son capteur Hasselblad 4/3 de 100 mégapixels, sa nacelle Infinity Gimbal et sa capacité à filmer en 6K. Il s’adresse clairement aux créateurs de contenu et aux vidéastes qui cherchent un outil polyvalent. C’est un drone premium qui n’est pas souvent en promotion, mais il fait aujourd’hui exception.
L’offre en cours sur le DJI Mavic 4 Pro
- Un capteur Hasselblad 4/3 de 100 mégapixels et vidéo 6K/60 HDR
- La nacelle Infinity Gimbal pour des mouvements de caméra inédits
- Jusqu’à 51 minutes d’autonomie annoncées par batterie
Le DJI Mavic 4 Pro est affiché à 2 099 euros en temps normal. Avec le code promo CVE2 sur Joybuy, il passe à 1 879 euros, soit 220 euros d’économie.
Si, par la suite, l’offre mentionnée dans cet article n’est plus disponible, merci de jeter un coup d’œil ci-dessous afin de dénicher d’autres offres concernant le DJI Mavic 4 Pro. Le tableau s’actualise automatiquement.
Triple caméra et nacelle Infinity Gimbal : la nouvelle donne
Le gros morceau du Mavic 4 Pro, c’est son système à trois caméras. La principale embarque un capteur Hasselblad 4/3 de 100 mégapixels (équivalent 28 mm), accompagnée d’un téléobjectif moyen de 48 mégapixels (70 mm) et d’un téléobjectif de 50 mégapixels (168 mm). En photo, la latitude de recadrage est large. En vidéo, la caméra principale grimpe jusqu’en 6K à 60 images par seconde en HDR, avec du ralenti 4K à 120 images par seconde. Les profils D-Log et HLG en 10 bits facilitent l’étalonnage en post-production.
La nacelle Infinity Gimbal apporte elle aussi un vrai gain. Là où le Mavic 3 Pro imposait de repositionner le drone pour certains angles, le Mavic 4 Pro permet des rotations étendues et des prises de vue verticales natives, idéales pour les formats courts type Reels ou Shorts. La stabilisation reste solide, même si l’horizon peut légèrement décrocher par vent fort. Côté cadrage, c’est un gain de liberté assez net.
Autonomie et sécurité de vol : du concret sur le terrain
DJI annonce 51 minutes d’autonomie, ce qui en fait l’un des drones grand public les plus endurants du marché. En conditions réelles, l’autonomie tombe plutôt entre 45 et 48 minutes selon le vent et le profil de vol, ce qui reste excellent pour enchaîner les prises sans stress. La recharge rapide via l’adaptateur 240 W associé au hub de charge (vendus séparément) permet de remettre trois batteries en service en environ 90 minutes.
Côté sécurité, le drone embarque six capteurs fisheye basse lumière et un LiDAR frontal, capable de détecter les obstacles même à 0,1 lux. Le retour au point de départ sans GPS fonctionne bien en conditions visuelles correctes. Petit bémol : l’absence de LiDAR arrière limite la protection omnidirectionnelle dans certaines situations. À noter aussi que ses 1 063 grammes le placent en catégorie C2, ce qui implique un enregistrement et une formation en ligne sur Alpha Tango pour voler en zone ouverte A2.
Pour tout savoir sur ses capacités en conditions réelles, nous vous conseillons de lire notre test du DJI Mavic 4 Pro, où chaque aspect technique est passé au crible.
Si vous souhaitez comparer ce modèle à d’autres appareils du même segment, notre guide des meilleurs drones photo et vidéo peut vous aider à faire le bon choix.

articles.title: MTN says South Africa's anti-immigrant attacks threaten Africa's digital future
articles.text:
As South Africa’s migration debate intensifies, MTN Group, Africa’s largest telco, is warning that anti-immigrant sentiment could have consequences beyond politics, affecting the movement of skills and businesses across Africa.
The telecoms giant has built one of Africa’s largest telecommunications businesses, connecting 312.7 million customers across 19 markets in Africa and the Middle East. With most of its growth coming from outside South Africa, the company is concerned that rising hostility targeting African migrants runs counter to the regional integration on which its business depends.
The developments have resonated across MTN’s footprint. Nigeria and Ghana, its largest markets, have joined Zimbabwe, Malawi and Eswatini in evacuating citizens from South Africa after the March and March Movement, an anti-immigration activist group, issued undocumented migrants with a June 30 deadline to leave the country.
At the Kgalema Motlanthe Foundation’s Winter Seminar on Thursday, which focused on migration, MTN executives made the business case for open borders. They argued that Africa’s future depends on creating economic opportunity, expanding digital connectivity and allowing skills and talent to move freely across the continent.
“If our discussion ends with the language of crisis around migration, we will have treated the symptom and missed the deeper challenge,” MTN Group President and chief executive officer (CEO) Ralph Mupita said. “People move because opportunity is unevenly distributed. The defining question is whether we can build economies in which mobility is matched by opportunity.”
The message comes as South Africa has witnessed months of attacks on foreign-owned businesses, forced evictions of migrants and growing anti-immigration rhetoric ahead of November’s local government elections.
For a company that has built its growth on connecting Africans across borders, those developments have become impossible to ignore. Mupita deliberately framed his own migration story as part of MTN’s identity.
“I also want to admit that I’m a migrant, 35 years in South Africa,” he told the audience. “I’m from Zimbabwe… My surname, Mupita, means ‘the one who moves from place to place.’” He described having relatives across Zimbabwe, Mozambique, Malawi and Angola before concluding: “So that’s who I am. I’m an African.”
For Mupita, the personal story reflected MTN’s own pan-African journey.
“I happen to be an African who is a steward… of an organisation that was born in South Africa,” he said, recalling that one of Nelson Mandela, the global democracy icon’s, earliest decisions after democracy was issuing the mobile licences in September 1993 that led to MTN’s creation. Today, that company has become Africa’s largest telecommunications operator.
Its success, Mupita argued, is inseparable from Africa’s prosperity.
“The future of Africa will not be determined by the borders that separate us, but by the economic opportunities that connect us,” he said. “Governments must set predictable policy and regulations. Businesses will follow and allocate resources and capital. Together, we can build a continent where opportunity is more evenly shared, and prosperity is more widely created.”
Mcebisi Jonas, the MTN Chairman, said immigration has become a convenient political scapegoat for South Africa’s deeper economic problems. “Our markets are in Africa. Our opportunities are in Africa. Our future is in Africa,” Jonas said. “South Africa cannot present itself as open for investment while treating African workers and traders with hostility. It sends a contradictory message: Africans are welcome as customers and investors, but not as people.”
Jonas stated that removing migrants would do nothing to solve South Africa’s economic challenges. “South Africa’s economic crisis is a product of weak growth, poor governance, inadequate education outcomes, infrastructure failures and structural inequality. If every foreign national left the country tomorrow, those problems would remain,” he said.
He added that South Africa continues to lose skilled citizens through emigration while making it difficult for skilled foreigners to stay, a contradiction he believes undermines the country’s competitiveness in a technology-driven economy.
The seminar’s broader message was that migration cannot be separated from Africa’s economic transformation.
Dr Ishmael Yamson, chairman of MTN Ghana’s board, said Africa’s demographic boom will only translate into prosperity if governments invest aggressively in digital capabilities. “Africa’s future competitiveness will depend on how successfully we equip young people with digital skills, entrepreneurial skills, technical skills and leadership capabilities,” noted Yamson. “The demographic dividend must become a skills dividend.”
True scale demands moving beyond surface-level integrations to robust execution. articles.title: EEUU está acusando a China de plagiar los modelos de Anthropic. Tenemos tres problemas con esa acusación
articles.text:
Michael Kratsios, asistente del presidente de EEUU, no se mordía la lengua esta semana cuando afirmaba que "Tenemos información que indica que Moonshoot AI destiló Fable de Anthropic para el desarrollo de su modelo K3". O lo que es lo mismo, acusan a China de plagiar el modelo de IA avanzado de la empresa estadounidense. Hay varios problemas fundamentales con esa acusación. Veámoslos.
Miedo a Kimi K3. Este modelo acaba de irrumpir en la escena IA con una fuerza arrolladora. Los benchmarks demuestran que Kimi K3 es uno de los mejores modelos de IA del mundo, con un rendimiento cercano a Fable 5 y GPT-5.6, los mejores modelos públicos de Anthropic y de OpenAI. Ese hito ha disparado su popularidad entre usuarios y empresas, y también las alarmas de Washington. La consecuencia inmediata ha sido de hecho política, porque desde la Administración Trump se habla ya abiertamente de sanciones por "robo de tecnología" si se confirma la acusación.
La acusación. En su texto Kratsios explica el supuesto mecanismo usado por Moonshot AI para copiar su modelo. Afirma que la startup china habría construido una plataforma interna para hacer consultas masivas a modelos de EEUU, cambiando los métodos de acceso para evitar ser detectada y transfiriendo luego sus capacidades a Kimi K3. Añade además que la empresa ha logrado acceder a servidores con chips GB300 de Nvidia en países fuera de China para esquivar las restricciones de exportación.
¿Dónde están las pruebas? El primer problema que tenemos con ese discurso es que ya de primeras falta una pieza clave de ese discurso: Kratsios no acompaña esa acusación de evidencias técnicas. No da registros del uso, no da ejemplos de prompts y respuestas, ni tampoco patrones de consulta. Tampoco aporta análisis independientes que cualquier investigador podría revisar. Lo que tenemos ahora mismo es un relato y una acusación oficial, no una "infracción" demostrada.
La polémica sobre la destilación. La palabra clave de ese discurso es "destilación". En IA, destilar un modelo significa entrenar uno nuevo usando las respuestas de otro. El modelo "maestro" responde a miles o millones de preguntas, y el modelo "estudiante" aprende a imitar sus pautas de razonamiento con menor coste y tamaño. La propia industria describe la destilación como una técnica legítima y estándar cuando se aplica sobre modelos permitidos o propios. La línea roja aparece cuando se aplica a modelos de terceros, a gran escala y sin permiso, lo que según el Gobierno de EEUU es un robo de propiedad intelectual.
Pero delito, lo que se dice delito, no es. El segundo problema es que la declaración y la acusación ni se apoyan en ningún marco jurídico claro y definido. Ni EEUU ni China tienen en la actualidad una ley específica que diga en qué condiciones destilar un modelo rival es delito de propiedad intelectual. Puede que viole los términos de servicio de una API o que incluso acabe oteniendo información sensible de empresas, pero no hay jurisprudencia al respecto. De hecho, hasta hace poco el debate en EEU estaba en regular los modelos frontera de EEUU como Mythos, que se consideraban demasiado peligrosos. De repente el debate está ahora en sancionar la destilación de modelos. Todo va demasiado rápido, una vez más, para adaptar la legislación.
Hipocresía made in USA. El tercer gran problema que tenemos con esa acusación es que los grandes modelos estadounidenses —incluidos los de Anthropic— se han entrenado con conjuntos de datos masivos que mezclan sitios web, libros, código, artículos de prensa y otros materiales en los que una parte notable está protegida por el copyright. La propia Anthropic llegó a un acuerdo con la justicia estos días por esa razón, y a Meta se la descubrió robando terabytes de libros con copyright para entrenar sus modelos.
Doble vara de medir. En EEUU las empresas de IA se defienden argumentando que eso entra del "uso justo" del contenido, pero los autores ni dieron su permiso, ni cobraron por ello. Esa misma industria y ese mismo Gobierno que han sumido como normal entrenar modelos sobre contenido ajeno se quejan de que una startup china use las salidas de sus modelos para entrenar los suyos. No son prácticas idénticas, pero la doble vara de medir es difícil de ignorar.
La IA, una vez más, como arma. La administracion Trump está llevando esta cuestión a otra escala. Al acusar a Moonshot AI de usar chips restringidos y de desarrollar Kimi K3 destilando Fable 5, sitúa la destilación en el mismo cajón que el espionaje industrial o el robo de secretos militares. La IA deja de ser un producto software y se convierte en un arma tecnológica estratégica. Y ahí no importa tanto aportar pruebas o ser precisos técnicamente: importa que lo que ha hecho China es un ataque a su (¿antigua?) hegemonía tecnológica.
Si este tipo de acusación os suena, tenéis buena memoria.

articles.title: Introducing Claude Opus 5 on AWS: Anthropic’s most capable Opus model | Amazon Web Services
articles.text:
Artificial Intelligence
Introducing Claude Opus 5 on AWS: Anthropic’s most capable Opus model
Today, we announce the availability of Claude Opus 5 on Amazon Bedrock and Claude Platform on AWS. Claude Opus 5 is Anthropic’s most advanced Opus model and the first in the fifth generation. It is a meaningful step forward, providing improvements across the workflows that teams run in production such as agentic coding, knowledge work, visual understanding, and long-running tasks. According to Anthropic, Claude Opus 5 matches Claude Fable 5’s top-tier intelligence in many domains at Opus-tier pricing.
On Amazon Bedrock, Claude Opus 5 benefits from zero data retention (ZDR) by default, delivering top-tier intelligence without compromising enterprise data governance. Claude Opus 5 is powered by Bedrock’s next-generation inference engine, letting you build within your existing AWS environment, maintain enterprise security and regional data residency, and scale inference with zero operator access.
Claude Opus 5 is also available through Claude Platform on AWS, which supports zero data retention on request and gives you access to Anthropic’s native platform experience and capabilities through the AWS Console. Build, test, and deploy with the same APIs, features, and console experience you get working with Anthropic directly, unified with AWS billing and authentication.
This post covers Opus 5’s improvements and practical guidance for AI engineers integrating the model into agentic systems and production inference workloads on Amazon Bedrock. See the documentation for Claude Platform on AWS.
What makes Claude Opus 5 different
According to Anthropic, Claude Opus 5 delivers a step-change in coding. It understands and navigates codebases like an experienced engineer and writes production-quality code while adapting its strategy as it works. It powers dependable long-running agents that work for hours and even overnight, finding paths around obstacles, recovering from errors, and reaching their objectives. For professional work, it brings deeper reasoning to long documents and higher accuracy to complex analysis, with the largest gains on document-heavy enterprise tasks. Together, this adds up to frontier capability at Opus-tier economics.
Use cases
Claude Opus 5 is a strong fit for industries where precision, reliability, and deep reasoning matter most. For financial services teams, it powers financial workflows with deeper reasoning and end-to-end understanding of context. It handles compliance-sensitive work with more clarity and focus. For agent and workflow automation, it pushes back on flawed instructions and breaks complex jobs into sub-agents that need less oversight. In productivity work, it handles report building and auditing, document drafting, and structured analysis with high consistency. It runs multi-day projects and produces professional-grade outputs.
Claude Opus 5 also improves on Claude Opus 4.8’s cyber capabilities across the board, from coding to cyber security. In higher-risk areas, Opus 5 may fall back to Opus 4.8. Users are notified when this happens, and fallbacks can be configured when using the APIs.
Getting started with Claude Opus 5 on Amazon Bedrock
You can get started with Claude Opus 5 in the Amazon Bedrock console.
In the Amazon Bedrock console, under Test, choose Playground.
For the model, choose Claude Opus 5. Now, you can test your complex coding prompt with the model.
Amazon Bedrock console Playground with Claude Opus 5 selected
You can also access the model programmatically using the Anthropic Messages API to call bedrock-runtime through the Anthropic SDK or bedrock-mantle endpoints, or keep using the Invoke and Converse API on bedrock-runtime through the AWS Command Line Interface (AWS CLI) and AWS SDK.
Prerequisites
- Active AWS account with Amazon Bedrock access.
- AWS CLI installed and configured.
- Python 3.8+.
- Boto3 installed: pip install boto3
- Anthropic SDK installed: pip install anthropic[bedrock]
- IAM permissions: bedrock:InvokeModel,bedrock:InvokeModelWithResponseStream, andbedrock:CreateInference
Here’s a quick example using the AWS SDK for Python (Boto3):
You can also use Claude Opus 5 with the Amazon Bedrock Converse API for a unified multi-model experience:
You can also use Claude Opus 5 with the Anthropic Messages API using the anthropic[bedrock] SDK package for a streamlined experience:
Claude Opus 5 supports adding and removing tools mid-conversation through tool_addition and tool_removal content blocks on role: "system" messages, instead of re-sending the full top-level tools array. See Bedrock documentation for more details.
Availability
Claude Opus 5 is available today on Amazon Bedrock in Regions including US East (N. Virginia), Asia Pacific (Melbourne), Europe (Ireland), and Europe (Stockholm). See Bedrock documentation for the full list of supported Regions. Claude Opus 5 is also available on the Claude Platform on AWS in North America, South America, Europe, and Asia Pacific.
Give Claude Opus 5 a try in the Amazon Bedrock console, in Claude Platform on AWS, or explore the Getting Started notebooks on GitHub. You can also unlock the full potential of Opus 5 by using Advanced Prompt Optimization on Amazon Bedrock. It takes your current prompts, benchmarks them against your evaluation criteria, and outputs production-ready rewrites.

articles.title: Could Grand Theft Auto 6 run well on Switch 2? — Someone has seemingly ported Grand Theft Auto 5 to the original Switch, giving us an idea of what to expect, but performance appears lacking
articles.text:
It looks like someone has managed to get Grand Theft Auto 5 running on an original Switch, and now I'm wondering what GTA 6 could look like on Switch 2
Is the Switch 2 powerful enough to withstand GTA 6?
- Someone may have ported Grand Theft Auto 5 to Nintendo Switch
- Performance appears poor and reaches 22FPS at most
- It makes me wonder what Grand Theft Auto 6 could look like running on Switch 2
While we wait for Grand Theft Auto 6, someone has seemingly managed to port Grand Theft Auto 5 to the Nintendo Switch.
The port was apparently created by M0jso and posted to Reddit, where footage apparently shows a native v2699 (2023) version of the 13-year-old game, running on the original Switch, albeit rather poorly.
The performance overlay shows that the frame rate reaches 22FPS at most, and declines to 11FPS in some places, but it does appear to be playable.
A user explained that the footage had been taken down a while ago, but it looks like the project is in progress again. M0jso showcased more videos on X, explaining that rendering can be broken in some places, crashes are frequent, but they have seemingly managed to play GTA 5 on a real Switch console.
However, overall, performance appears poor, and the odds of the game reaching console or PC-level quality seem slim. It made me wonder what GTA 6 could look like running on the Nintendo Switch 2, a more advanced system that boasts 4K and 1440p resolutions and 60FPS.
For now, Rockstar hasn't shared any plans to port the game to Switch 2 - a PC version hasn't been announced either - but we've seen demanding games such as Cyberpunk 2077 and Hogwarts Legacy functioning on the console with minor frame rate issues.
That being said, GTA 6 will be a massive game, with a map possibly even bigger than Cyberpunk 2077 and GTA 5's. Not to mention the dense locations and level of detail that PS5 and Xbox Series X will also need to contend with.

While the game's performance features haven't been revealed yet, reports have claimed that it's likely to run at 30FPS on PS5 consoles due to CPU limitations, which could make the likelihood of a Switch 2 port rather slim.
According to Digital Foundry, GTA 6 running at 60FPS on current-gen might be pushing it, but a 40FPS mode could be possible.
There's still just under five months to go before the game launches on November 19, so we could learn more about performance, potential graphics modes, and even get a third trailer soon.

articles.title: Why player trust is becoming Europe’s next iGaming growth layer (Sponsored) | EU-Startups
articles.text:
For years, European iGaming growth has been driven by better products, faster payments, and expansion into new markets.
These things still matter, but they’re not enough on their own anymore. Players now see the same types of games, bonuses, and payment options almost everywhere. So, what really makes a difference is whether you trust the brand to treat you fairly after you sign up.
The market backdrop makes this shift commercially significant. According to the European Gaming and Betting Association, European gambling gross gaming revenue reached roughly €123.4 billion in 2024, up around 5% year on year, with online channels taking an ever larger share.
In their global gambling market analysis, H2 Gambling Capital projects the European market will grow from about €154.8 billion ($177 billion) in 2024 to €206.4 billion ($236 billion) by 2030.
In a market that size and that competitive, small differences in whether players stay, deposit again, and recommend a brand translate into very large revenue differences, and those differences increasingly hinge on trust.
Most players want to know if they’ll get their money out easily, if the bonus rules are clear, if their personal details are safe, and if support will actually help when it matters. If any of this is confusing, people hesitate to play. That means fewer deposits and more players leaving for other sites.
For operators, trust is now about more than just following the rules. It affects how well they keep players, handle payments, work with regulators, and build their reputation across Europe.
Trust now sits inside the product
Europe’s gambling market is not governed by one rulebook. Each country regulates online gambling through its own framework.
That structure lets regulators respond to local risks. But for players, it can create an uneven experience. Someone moving between brands and markets may face different verification steps, bonus rules, withdrawal timelines, and support standards.
As a result, trust is part of the product. Players judge an operator when they read bonus terms, set limits, upload documents, request a withdrawal, or contact support. Each moment either makes the platform feel reliable or creates doubt.
A brand’s appearance may be professional, but unclear payout processes, complaint procedures, or bonus conditions can erode trust before the first deposit.
Because standards vary across markets, many players now use sites like Casinomeister, a casino review and player-advocacy platform, to research verification procedures, withdrawal experiences, dispute histories, and bonus terms before choosing an operator.
The retention mechanics that actually move the needle
When operators look closely at why players churn, the causes are rarely the games themselves. They cluster around a handful of concrete product and payments mechanisms, and each one is fixable:
- Onboarding and KYC: front-loaded identity verification (document and address checks completed at sign-up rather than at the first cash-out) removes the single most common point of frustration, because players are not surprised by verification requests when they finally try to withdraw.
- Payout rails: instant or same-day withdrawals via account-to-account methods such as open banking and Trustly, or e-wallets, consistently outperform slower card and bank-transfer routes on repeat-deposit behaviour. The speed of the second withdrawal is often what decides whether a player becomes a regular.
- Bonus-term clarity: showing wagering requirements, game weightings, maximum bet caps, and expiry dates before a player opts in reduces disputes and chargebacks, which are a direct drag on payment relationships and retention.
- Safer-gambling tooling: deposit limits, reality checks, cool-off periods, and self-exclusion that are easy to find and set build long-term confidence and reduce the regulatory and reputational shocks that cause sudden player loss.
None of these are marketing features. They are operational levers that determine whether a player deposits a second and third time, which is where profitability in a mature market is won.
Regulators are raising expectations
The shift is also visible in regulation. European regulators have become more active around advertising, safer gambling, customer checks, and AML controls.
Operators are expected to identify risks earlier, explain processes more clearly, protect vulnerable users, and demonstrate that growth is built on sound controls.
An operator might get lots of deposits at first, but that doesn’t last if complaints rise or payments are delayed. Stronger standards help avoid fines, payment issues, and player losses. Following the rules isn’t just about avoiding trouble; it also helps create a smoother experience for everyone.
Withdrawals are the main trust test
The clearest test comes when a player tries to cash out. Deposits often feel instant. Withdrawals rarely do, because operators still need to verify identity, check for fraud, review funding sources, and meet anti-money laundering requirements.
Those checks are legitimate. But when they are poorly explained, even a routine review can feel suspicious. The problem is not always the delay itself. It is the uncertainty around the delay.
A player is more likely to remain patient when the process is clear. Strong operators make the cash-out journey clearer by showing players:
- Why is a document needed
- Which file formats are accepted
- How long does a review usually take
- Which bonus rule may affect the payout
- Where to get a real update
Bonus terms can create the same friction. When limits, restricted games, caps, or expiry dates are unclear, disputes become more likely. Strong operators reduce that risk by making key rules clear before players commit money.
Safer gambling now shapes reputation
Withdrawal transparency sits inside a wider trust question: how operators protect players as they play.
Safer gambling tools, once hidden, are now prominent. Regulators, media, banks, partners, and players all monitor how effectively brands implement deposit limits, time-outs, self-exclusion, risk monitoring, and support. These features are now integral to the player experience.
When operators fail to protect vulnerable users, regulators often respond with stricter controls. Advertising bans and tougher customer monitoring reflect public concern about harm.
Those measures were driven by trust, not weak product design. The best systems make it easy to find, use, and understand safer choices.
The next layer of growth will be earned
The iGaming industry in Europe still has significant potential for expansion. Demand will continue to be shaped by mobile play, live casino formats, customisation, and the entrance of regulated markets.
But the next layer of growth will not come from reach alone. It will come from players confident enough to deposit, return, withdraw, and recommend a brand to others.
Trust is practical. It appears in fewer disputes, faster support resolution, smoother verification, cleaner license reviews, stronger payment relationships, and better retention.
Winning operators will publish clearer terms, communicate openly, improve cash-out routes, respond faster to issues, and make safer gambling tools easier to use without restricting play.
In an established European market, growth will increasingly depend on whether players trust an operator before their first deposit and continue to trust it after their first withdrawal.

articles.title: AI firms want more data centers; Trump's EPA may give neighbors less say
articles.text:
The Trump administration is quietly considering a rule change that could make it easier for polluters to build facilities—including certain gas plants and diesel generators that power data centers—with little to no notice to the public.
On Wednesday, the Environmental Protection Agency held a public hearing on a proposed rule change that would hand the power to states to decide how the public participates in the permitting process for certain new sources of air pollution. The proposed rollback comes as data centers face greater pushbackacross the US, with many communities using the permitting process to try to slow down development. Any changes could have major consequences for how ordinary people are given notice about new or expanded polluting facilities coming into their neighborhoods.
“As someone actively working in communities with data centers, I know this to be fundamentally true: People want to have a say,” Vanessa Lynch, a Pennsylvania organizer with Moms Clean Air Force, said at the EPA hearing.
Companies building any kind of facilities that release air pollution are required to get permits under the Clean Air Act. Polluting sources can either be put through a “major” permitting process, meaning that they meet or exceed thresholds for certain pollutants, or a “minor” one for those that don’t.
Major sources of pollution are reviewed by both federal and state regulators and have extensive requirements before and after construction. However, there’s less oversight of minor sources. The scope of what gets permitted as a minor source is extremely broad and can include everything from dry cleaners and auto body shops to to diesel and gas engines. The latter two are increasingly being used to power data centers, with operators such as xAI and Meta using minor source permitting processes to build behind-the-meter gas plants.
